channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: At Pilsen Barber Shop’s Ponte Tus Moños Event, Elaborate Braids Are A Symbol Of Resistance
item.description: Organizers of Sunday’s event will raise funds for local immigrant groups by making braids, or trenzas, a symbol of cultural pride.

item.title: Chicago’s 1st Reentry Support Center For Formerly Incarcerated Women Opens In Pilsen
item.description: The Women's Justice Institute, a national center based in Chicago, was selected to run the city's first support center for women in or returning from prison.

item.title: SuSu, A Multi-Cultural Steakhouse, Coming To Fulton Market
item.description: SuSu’s menu, a blend of Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the Mediterranean, is influenced by chef Alexander Willis’ years spent living and working overseas.

item.title: Giggity, Giggity! ‘Family Guy’ Drunken Clam Bar Pops Up In Chicago
item.description: Fans of the popular animated series can visit familiar settings and enjoy a Quahog-inspired menu at Peter Griffin's favorite local hangout through April 19.

item.title: Chicago Public Schools Cancels Classes Friday Due To Extreme Cold
item.description: CPS has canceled classes Friday as temperatures are expected to drop below zero. All school buildings will be closed to the public, the district said in a news release.

item.title: Mama Africa’s Marketplace At Risk Of Closure As Veterans’ Nonprofit Prepares To Buy Building
item.description: The South Shore community hub and shop centered around African-made products could close by Friday. A GoFundMe by owner Lakeisha Ifarinu Williams aims to counter the nonprofit Leave No Veteran Behind and buy the property.

item.title: Polar Plunge Canceled This Weekend As Dangerous Cold Sets In, Organizer Says
item.description: The event, held annually in January, sees neighbors jump into Lake Michigan to raise money for charity. But conditions will be too extreme for the cold-weather event, organizers said.

item.title: Did Landlord Tip Off Immigration Raid At Troubled South Shore Building? The State Is Investigating
item.description: Illinois is using a housing discrimination charge to investigate claims that a landlord and property management used the feds to clear a building they struggled to maintain.

item.title: Chicago Crossing Guard Carries Students To Safety In Frigid Temps After Water Main Break
item.description: A slurry of icy water flooded the intersection of Bryn Mawr and California after a water main break, city officials said. But Jamieson Elementary School crossing guard Joe Sass saved the day.

item.title: Federal Judge Agrees To Dismiss Excessive Force Lawsuit Against Immigration Agents
item.description: The case, brought by Block Club Chicago and other media groups, forced federal officials to release hundreds of videos and temporarily limit force against journalists and protesters during Operation Midway Blitz.
